rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: cross-module sequencing front-run (e.g. naming a skill in M2 that spoils M3's reveal) is the rule's target. This file is a training-wide 'moves' glossary — curriculum/CLAUDE.md types it as 'Quick reference — flat lookup. No progression', and its own maintainer note ('Sweep coverage', L385-387) states by design it surveys prompts across all of M1-M6 plus the full AE101-referenced exercise list, so cross-cutting is the deliberate shape, not an accident. Closest-to-violating line: L161, the 'Skill by name' entry — 'Skills register at install time and Claude addresses them by name: `access-control-analysis`, `stride`, `test-strategy`.' Per the AE101 strategy doc (M3 in detail, M1 in detail), M3 owns 'the first Skill use + first subagent + first authoring together — the right concentration', and M1 explicitly has none. So these three names are M3's primitive. It stays inside the rule because the reveal the naming would spoil is the functional identifier only (what you type to invoke a skill) — not M3's actual teaching moment, which is the access-surface delta the student is underweighting, the one threat worth hardening picked from STRIDE's six categories, and the authored skill's self-disclosed weak spot. A syllabus line or index entry naming a topic does not pre-empt the lesson built on top of it, and none of that lesson content leaks here. The exercise-slug examples elsewhere in the file (L322, L329, L340, L347, L354 — `ae101-m2-integrate-branch`, `ae101-m3-sharpen-skill`, `walk-and-send-off-2`, `ae101-m4-take-task-end-to-end`, `ae101-m5-rerun-packaged`, `author-test-strategy-skill-1`) name which exercise demonstrates a prompt-writing pattern, never what that exercise teaches or discovers — orthogonal to the module's content reveal. Diff since pin 28a4abc5 (`git diff 28a4abc5..HEAD`) touches only a closer's wording, a self-referential count-history clause, and the Quality-line addition — none of it sequencing-relevant, and this exact body (module-content-wise) already carries a strategy@28a4abc5 PASS.
